text:
olivia: Heads up: saw a correlated increase in pcie_uncorrectable + HBM_evictions on rack usw1-rk09. 95th token latency for several multi-tenant pods jumped. suspect one tenant running long sparse attention runs. thinking a light-touch mitigation first.

ben: I looked at the live flamegraphs. HBM churn + memcpy spikes line up with alloc-9212. Could try spot-throttling that alloc (reduce concurrency) before touching nodes.

marta: Agree. Draining racks killed our warm caches last month. Suggest: (1) rate-limit the offending alloc to 50% for 4m, (2) if no improvement, move non-reserved dev traffic to reserve-slices in same region if available, (3) as last resort soft-cordon the host.

olivia: Can we use a serving-layer micropolicy to drop KV population for that alloc to reduce churn? That avoids routing changes.

ben: Yes, serving supports an "hbmlimit" flag to skip KV fills; toggling it reduces HBM pressure significantly. I'll flip to hbmlimit=true for alloc-9212 as trial.

marta: Note: if we flip hbmlimit, output quality for that tenant may degrade for some prompts. Need to notify tenant owners. Is there a quick notification channel?

olivia: ops-bot:notify @alloc-owners/9212 -> sent.

deploy-bot: notification delivered to alloc-owners/9212.

ben: hbmlimit=true applied. Watching metrics.

marta: Also mark the host with annotation infra/no-evict so autoscaler won't pre-scale-down warm pool during mitigation.

olivia: Good call. Commands I ran: kubectl annotate node usw1-rk09-07 infra/no-evict=true && servingctl set-alloc-flag alloc-9212 hbmlimit=true.

ben: Metrics: HBM_evictions down ~50% in 60s, pcie_uncorrectable down ~30%, tail latency down ~28%. This looks promising.

marta: Great. Let's keep hbmlimit for 10m and then re-evaluate. If it returns, plan B: move dev weight to reserve-slices (prefer same-az) with TTL 15m. Pre-warm reserve slices with small traffic to avoid cold spikes.

olivia: Cost tradeoff: pre-warm adds ~0.3% cost for the region for 15m. Acceptable.

ben: I'll also create a short-lived sigpipe alert that triggers auto-throttle if pcie_uncorrectable > 5/min for a sliding 3m window. Low false-positive risk.

marta: +1 on alert. Also add a follow-up ticket to have Optimize recommend lower-memory variants for model families that cause HBM churn. infra#1901.

olivia: For the postmortem: let's capture the exact sequence, toggling hbmlimit avoided a node drain and saved estimated 4% token-cost for the hour.

deploy-bot: alert rule created: noisy-rack-auto-throttle-7051230000. ticket created: infra#1901.

ben: Status: hbmlimit active, autoscaler safe-guard in place, reserve pre-warm queued but not executed. Recheck in 10m.

marta: Thanks. If hbmlimit causes customer complaints, we'll revert and go to the routing fallback. Closing thread for now.
